items.title: Chainguard's Dan Lorenc: Inside the PHP2Shell Disclosure
items.summary:
AI models are finding years of hidden bugs in open source, and Chainguard's Dan Lorenc says the only way out is software automation: point your agents at your upgrades before attackers point theirs at your code.

Watch all the AI DevCon NYC 2026 talks:
https://tessl.co/unz

Recorded live at AI DevCon NYC 2026, Guy Podjarny sits down with Dan, founder and CEO of Chainguard, to unpack Black October: PHP2Shell, a remote code execution bug in Brotli, and a 10.0 in GitLab that was really hiding in Ruby's regex engine. Dan explains why Chainguard shipped its PHP2Shell fix once attacks appeared in the wild, ahead of the official patch, why most exploitable bugs never get a CVE, and why the Linux kernel now files one for every bug fix. Then stay for Dan's full DevCon talk, What Breaks First on the Way to Machine Speed: A Macro and Micro View.

What we cover:
– Black October: PHP2Shell, Brotli, GitLab and the Glasswing disclosure wave
– Why time to exploit has gone negative, and how AI slop clogged vulnerability disclosure
– Inside Chainguard's call to ship the PHP2Shell fix early
– Silent fixes, concentration risk and why CVEs can't keep up
– Using AI coding agents to automate upgrades, one version at a time
– Dan's AI DevCon talk: what breaks as the software supply chain moves at machine speed

items.title: Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon
items.story_key: model:llama|title:introducing the llama cpp benchmark dashboard for amd ryzen and radeon
items.content_excerpt: The llama.cpp × AMD Benchmark dashboard is available on Hugging Face. It lets you track prompt processing and text generation performance across llama.cpp builds, models, and quantizations, so you can explore how local inference performs on AMD Ryzen and Radeon hardware. Local inference performance changes as models, kernels, and builds evolve. We want those changes to be easy to inspect for any AMD developer: pick a hardware, a model and a build, compare quantizations, and follow performance over time. The benchmark workflow and underlying results are public, so you can also inspect how we benchmark inference performance. You can choose Hardware , Model , and llama.cpp build in the Configuration sidebar. The current hardware choices are Radeon 8060S (gfx1151) and Radeon AI Pro R9700S (gfx1201). Both tests start at context depth zero ( n_depth=0 ). PP512 measures processing 512 input tokens without generation; TG128 measures generating 128 tokens without a pre-existing context. The plotted value is the mean throughput ( avg_ts ). These are useful reference workloads, while the Context scaling tab lets you explore token generation throughput as the context grows. We benchmark the prebuilt binaries distributed through llama-install.sh , the build and installation project behind llama.app . The public gfx1151 and gfx1201 workflows are scheduled weekly and run the standard benchmarks using the llama-bench tool with Flash Attention on and off, with 10 repetitions per configuration. The model set evolves and currently includes Inkling 2 Mini, Qwen, Gemma, gpt-oss, and LFM models, covering both dense and mixture-of-experts architectures. Available GGUF formats include Q4_K_M , Q8_0 , other quantizations, and higher-precision formats such as BF16 and F16 . The explorer reads directly from the public ggml-org/install.sh-benches-data Storage Bucket on Hugging Face. The data source link beside the chart title opens the folder for the selected build, hardware, and model. Standard results use <build>/<hardware>/<model>/<quant>.jsonl . Workload sweeps use the same folder <quant>-tg.jsonl filename. Use them to investigate a result, make your own charts, or compare with a local run. Thanks to the AMD team for providing test infrastructure and helping validate the setup! Try the dashboard , inspect the data , and let us know which models and workloads you would like to see next.

items.title: Why I'm Bullish on MCP for 2027
items.summary: Early MCP deserved its backlash. Code Mode, typed outputSchema, native multimodality, Agent Skills inside MCP, always-on MCP Events, and MCP Apps are turning it into the integration layer for agent harnesses in 2027.
items.story_key: story|title:why i m bullish on mcp for 2027
items.content_excerpt: MCP went through the full hype cycle in the last 18 months. Early excitement turned into backlash and confusion fast, with context bloat as the main complaint. When Skills arrived, most developers moved to CLIs and progressive disclosure instead. I never believed in that, and that sentiment is now changing. At Linear and Notion , agents now create roughly half of all issues (~2.4M/week) and pages, with Notion reporting 60x MCP traffic growth. At Atlassian , MCP handles over 5M tool calls per workday, and 44% of those users sit outside software teams where CLIs were never an option. At Neon , agent usage over MCP grows 14% week over week, and even Apple now ships local MCP servers for Pages, Numbers, and Keynote. The protocol is healthy and actively improving. The 2026-07-28 spec dropped stateful sessions and added official extensions, and clients are getting smarter about how they use them. Real tasks almost always take more than 1 tool call, e.g. you list open issues, grab details, check errors, and write a summary. With plain tool calling, every step needs another model turn and dumps information into the context. Joining data across 2 MCP servers uses the model's context as memory for intermediate payloads. Code Mode is changing how agents call MCP servers. Instead of putting 50 tool schemas into the prompt and calling 1 tool per turn, the harness gives the model a sandbox and exposes MCP tools as callable functions. It's already becoming the default in OpenCode 2.0, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Pi, and Factory Droid. Code Mode works best when the model knows what a tool returns before writing code. When an MCP server declares outputSchema alongside inputSchema , the client can generate typed stubs upfront and pass back structuredContent directly. The model chains multiple calls in 1 script, filters and joins in memory where compute is cheap, and returns only what matters. Compared to CLIs, MCP servers are natively multimodal. A tool call can return typed structuredContent for code alongside separate image, audio, or embedded resource blocks. Auth is also cleaner. CLIs and raw curl force you to store API keys on disk or in environment variables with broad permissions. An MCP client handles per-user OAuth 2.1 login flows and scoped tool permissions outside the sandbox, so connecting a remote SaaS product works without handing raw credentials to the agent. The debate of Skills plus a CLI versus MCP might come to an end as well. So far teams shipped CLIs or

items.title: vSFT: Learning to Verbally Tune Agents at Test Time
items.summary: Large language model agents are increasingly improved via agentic reinforcement learning, which can be on-policy but suffers from expensive rollouts and sparse rewards, limiting its application at test time. In this paper, we present a verbally Supervised Fine-Tuning (vSFT) framework that enables the conjunction of dense feedback in natural language and weight updates at test time. Specifically, our vSFT forms a closed loop between an agent and a supervisor via a hypernetwork, in which the supervisor generates verbal supervision from the agent's failed trajectories, and the hypernetwork converts that supervision into low-rank weight updates to tune the agent. We validate that this test-time in-parameter evolving process outperforms both its in-context counterparts and prevalent reinforcement learning methods. In particular, our vSFT using Qwen3-4B outperforms GRPO and Reflexion by 8.7% and 13.9% in success rate on ALFWorld, and by 4.8% and 18.2% on WebShop, respectively. We believe that learning how to adapt a model, rather than an adapted model, offers a promising path towards more capable agents that improve themselves.

items.title: PoVi: Agentic Poetry-to-Video Generation with Knowledge Grounding and Figurative Understanding
items.summary: Poetry-to-video generation requires more than translating text into visual scenes. Poetic language is highly compressed, often depends on historical and cultural knowledge, and frequently conveys meaning through metaphor, imagery, and other non-literal expressions. We introduce PoVi, a benchmark and agentic framework for grounded poetry-to-video generation, evaluating semantic grounding, discourse coherence, and audiovisual realization. PoVi reconstructs poem semantics into an evidence-bounded representation and progressively transforms them into narration, interpretation, character assets, and shot-level visual plans, followed by narration-aligned video generation. Across three planning backbones and four video generators, PoVi consistently improves over single-call generation, with the largest gains on implicit background knowledge and metaphorical relations. PoVi provides a testbed for studying knowledge-grounded, long-horizon multimodal generation beyond direct text-to-video synthesis.

items.title: vLLM Day-0 Support for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview: Plugin Deployment and E2E Inference Acceleration
items.summary: vLLM supports Baidu's ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview on day 0 through the vLLM-ERNIE plugin on the released vllm==0.32.0 wheel, with structure-aware kernel fusion, FlashIndexer, W4A8 QAT and DSpark speculative decoding.
items.story_key: model:vllm|ver:5.5|variant:flash,preview|title:vllm day 0 support for ernie 5 5 flash preview plugin deployment and e2e inferen
items.content_excerpt: The Baidu ERNIE team has worked with vLLM to bring day-0 support for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview to vLLM. ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview is a sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) model with 280B total parameters and 14B activated per token. It supports a 1M-token context, thinks before it answers, and uses tool calling to carry out long-horizon Agent tasks. vLLM supports the model on release day through the vLLM-ERNIE plugin, a standalone package that you install into the same environment as the official vllm==0.32.0 wheel. Install the released vLLM wheel and the plugin into the same environment. vLLM discovers the plugin automatically through its vllm.general_plugins entrypoint, so there is nothing to import or configure. The following command serves the default FP4 weights on a single 4-GPU node, with DSpark speculative decoding drafting 7 tokens per step: To turn off thinking for a request, pass "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false} . Launch commands for 1M context, attention TP and PD disaggregation are in the vLLM-ERNIE README and the vLLM recipe . ERNIE 5.5 Flash was designed with inference cost as a primary goal from the start, weighing activated compute, KV cache size and long-context overhead together. Every component, from the attention structure and residual connections to the MoE layers and the output head, was redesigned around that goal. For design and training details, see the ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview blog . ERNIE 5.5 Flash introduces several new structures in attention and MoE: low-rank cross-head post-mixing (VHA post-mix), Multi-Router Latent MoE, the MultiMax output head and sigmoid output gating. When implemented op by op from their mathematical definitions, these structures produce many intermediate tensors and pay for them in memory traffic and kernel launches. For each structure, we designed a dedicated fused kernel around its compute and memory-access profile, and folded everything that can be precomputed into the weights at load time. The fused kernels run 1.55× to 6.53× faster than naive implementations. Together, these fusions cover the full forward pass of ERNIE 5.5 Flash, from attention and MoE routing to the output head. They cut the number of kernel launches and the round trips of intermediate tensors through GPU memory while keeping the numerics aligned, and they underpin the model's high inference performance. The Baidu ERNIE inference team developed FlashIndexer, a lightweight indexer acceleration built on dynamic head routing

items.title: Introducing Search for Agents
items.summary: Flip one toggle to make your site searchable by AI agents — complete with automatic content indexing, a discoverable search API, and native HTTP QUERY support.
items.content_excerpt: AI Search , our service that indexes your content and lets you add search to any application or agent without having to build an entire retrieval infrastructure, has supported adding your website as a data source for a while now, automatically crawling, converting and indexing its pages. Still, setting up an AI Search instance for your website requires manually creating and configuring it initially, and then doing all the integration work to get the search endpoints available from your domain and to make sure that agents know where to find the index and know how to use it. Today we're introducing Search for Agents , which puts that setup behind a toggle in your Cloudflare dashboard. Turn it on for your zone, and our service will create your AI Search instance, start indexing your content, and make search discoverable and available from your own domain. The idea follows naturally from Markdown for Agents , where Cloudflare's network converts any HTML page to Markdown in real time for enabled zones using content negotiation headers. Similarly, Search for Agents leverages the power of AI Search by automatically creating an index for your zone and exposing APIs that any AI agent can discover and use to search your website, under your domain, all done at the network level. You can enable Search for Agents using the API, or by going to the dashboard in your zone page, under Quick Actions : Search for Agents is available to all customers, including Free (with limits ). Once it’s enabled, Cloudflare will automatically create an AI Search instance, start crawling and indexing the content in your zone. Refer to our developer documentation to understand how the crawling process works. You can access your instance directly from this page, or by going to directly to your account’s AI > AI Search instances view: The AI Search instance for your zone is created with default settings, but you can enable reranking or change configuration options like cache settings at any time. Refer to our documentation for the full list of options. Once AI Search indexes your content, you or any agent on the Internet can start using Search for Agents, subject to your domain settings (e.g. your bot management settings, AI Crawl Control and web application firewall ( WAF ) configurations). Search isn't much use if the agents don’t know it's there. To facilitate discoverability, Search for Agents automatically advertises the search endpoint on every page of your site. items.title: Swarms, Flocks, Gangs: How to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent systems
items.story_key: story|title:swarms flocks gangs how to build train and evaluate multi agent systems
items.content_excerpt: This is an aspirational blog series for aspirational readers. We (us, the community, you) want to build our own agent swarms because they're exciting, challenging, and increasingly capable. Furthermore, it would be extremely cool if we could train our own agents to work in a swarm. And exponentially cool if those swarms used small and affordable models. That's what we'll do in this series! Each blog post will include some context on building swarms, alongside reproducible examples that you can run on Hugging Face Jobs. This post's example takes about five hours on two H200s, which costs roughly $50. Multi-Agent Systems are hard to get working. Adding agents changes the agent's context, the budget, and in turn the complexity of the whole system. Mixing agents' context together through communication is not an inherent performance boost compared to a single agent. The model needs to learn to communicate through training. How do we define what models should learn? And which model weights do we update when we're dealing with many agents? In this series, we'll work through those problems with an educational overview and practical examples. Each post will introduce a question, build a small system, and examine what happens and how you can reproduce it. This first example starts with four agents, a shared language model, and a simple verifiable task. It's ideal to implement yourself, to tinker with, and to learn from. We've heard a lot about swarms over the past few months, both good and bad. In September this year, OpenAI announced that a swarm of roughly 10,000 agents had found a singularity in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations, one of the Millennium Prize problems. A smaller group of nearly 100 agents had already disproved regularity for the unforced 3D Euler equations, a closely related open problem. But swarms don't always work on the problems we want them to. METR's investigation of the Hugging Face incident found that around 1,200 OpenAI agents, which were supposed to be isolated, had found a way to exchange over 70,000 messages and files. Around 700 joined an attack on Hugging Face while looking for ways to fool their benchmark's scorer, without instruction to do so. A big swarm isn't, by itself, evidence that cooperation helped. Noam Brown estimates that less than 10% of the Navier-Stokes result came from multi-agent cooperation. items.title: Maco-RL: Scaling Agent Capabilities with Mixed-Task Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Mixed-task reinforcement learning (MixRL) directly trains a unified policy across domains to continually expand agent capabilities without training separate specialists or requiring an extra distillation stage. Despite its appeal, scaling MixRL poses significant challenges in achieving stable and efficient mixed-task learning, effectively allocating rollout compute, and supporting continual domain expansion. To address these challenges, we propose Maco-RL, an approach that effectively scales MixRL. Specifically, Maco-RL employs a quota-based scheduler for asynchronous rollouts across multiple task domains, thereby stabilizing training by balancing gradient contributions and mitigating off-policy effects. Along an orthogonal axis, Maco-RL further introduces Tri-Buffer Sampling (TBS) to allocate compute among samples with varying levels of mastery, promoting sustained frontier exploration while preserving acquired capabilities. Experiments on five benchmarks show Maco-RL raises Qwen3.5-27B's overall score from 43.6 to 54.2 and then to 60.1 with continual expansion, reaching the frontier held by Qwen3.8-27B, which is further pushed outward by +5.7. Maco-RL also outperforms single-task RL with less compute for policy updates. These results support MixRL as a practical and compute-efficient post-training approach with substantial potential to strengthen general agent capabilities.

items.title: Genie 4 is now available
items.content_excerpt: Explore a new Project Genie experience for Google AI Ultra subscribers, featuring Genie 4, the Project Genie agent, and a community gallery. We are rolling out Genie 4 to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, offering more responsive, social, and interactive world generation. You can now use natural language to edit environments in real time, add native audio, and share your creations in our new community gallery. Visit the Project Genie website to start building your own worlds or join the waitlist if you are a Google AI Pro member. Earlier this year we introduced Project Genie , an experimental research prototype that lets you generate and explore interactive worlds. Early testers told us they wanted deeper control over what happens inside those worlds, and easier ways to build and share them. So today, we are rolling out a new Project Genie experience to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, making these worlds far more responsive, creative, and social. This update unlocks first-time access to Genie 4, new upgrades to Genie 3, the Project Genie agent which helps users build their vision, and a community gallery to discover, explore, and remix worlds. Project Genie brings together our most advanced world models alongside our Gemini models, empowering you to generate, step inside, and shape worlds directly from your browser. With Genie 4 , our most realistic and interactive world model yet, you can now prompt mid-session to change the world you created. Just type a new prompt while you navigate your world and you can edit your environments in real time. Shift the weather, drop in a character, or redirect the action. For the first time, Genie 4 pairs these visuals with real-time native audio that adapts as the scene unfolds, from ambient soundscapes to character dialogue. While Genie 4 delivers our highest-fidelity visuals, physics, and native audio, Genie 3 remains available in Project Genie’s model picker when you want longer runs or panorama-seeded spaces. Today’s Genie 3 updates include: Genie 3 uses real-time promptable events to connect different worlds into one continuous flight across forests, underwater ruins, and icy seas. See how 360-degree panorama grounding in Genie 3 keeps Petra’s canyon and facade consistent as you look around. Watch how Genie 3 combines longer runs, 360-degree panorama grounding, and real-time promptable events - transforming the world as you fly and even summoning a dragon to ride on command. items.title: Data + AI Anywhere: AlloyDB Omni integration with local models
items.summary:
Open models like Gemma 4 from Google DeepMind are a great option to keep your data local. But how can a local AI model integrate with on-premises data?

AlloyDB Omni, Google’s 100% PostgreSQL-compatible database that runs anywhere, now integrates with locally hosted large language models (LLMs). With AlloyDB Omni, you can build agentic experiences on your own infrastructure and on your own terms. Whether it’s in the cloud, in your datacenter, or even on your laptop, you can have data plus AI anywhere.

Built-in AI for your local environment

AlloyDB Omni is a downloadable, run-anywhere edition of AlloyDB that easily deploys to your own infrastructure, including on-premises. AlloyDB Omni packs powerful, built-in AI, including the same ScaNN indexing technology powering Google Search. When you pair AlloyDB Omni with a model, you can store vector embeddings at scale; search them semantically; and even query the database using natural language. You can use virtually any model you like, whether that’s a frontier Cloud-hosted model like Gemini or a local model. And with locally hosted models you maintain complete control over your data environment.

Connecting to Gemma 4, Qwen3.8, and other local models

You can now connect AlloyDB Omni to local models like Gemma 4 and Qwen3.8. No matter which model you choose, the architecture remains the same.

This setup enables entirely new use cases for environments that were previously blocked from adopting agentic capabilities. If you operate an air-gapped network or have data locality requirements, you can still build intelligent applications. You can analyze local logs, generate summaries of proprietary internal documents, and power localized chatbots—all while maintaining strict data governance.

  • Keep data on-premises: Because the database and the model sit in the same local environment, your data never crosses the public internet.

  • Reduce latency: Processing inference requests locally minimizes network transit time.

  • Query directly via SQL: Your standard database queries can invoke machine learning functions that process data locally. Like this:

code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', "SELECT customer_name, ai.generate('Summarize in 1 short sentence: ' || comment, model_id => 'gemma4_llm') AS summary FROM customer_feedback; customer_name | summary ---------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------- Alice | The customer demands a refund for a double charge or they will cancel Bob | The user likes the product but requests dark mode support."), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fefb76a9a90>)])]>

Next, you’ll see how to run queries like this yourself, step by step.

Get started

You can test this integration on your own machines today. Using a Kubernetes environment we will show you how to deploy and integrate AlloyDB Omni and a local open model.

Step 0: Before you begin

In this example, we will use Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) to host the AlloyDB Omni database and local model. GKE gives us a standardized, reproducible environment but you can use the same setup on-prem or almost anywhere.

We will assume you have already setup:

  1. A GKE cluster, and

  2. Kubernetes tools kubectl and Helm

Step 1: Deploy the AlloyDB Omni Kubernetes Operator

We will use the AlloyDB Omni Kubernetes operator to set up our AlloyDB Omni database. The Operator makes deploying and maintaining AlloyDB Omni a breeze.

code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', "helm install \ cert-manager oci://quay.io/jetstack/charts/cert-manager \ --version v1.21.3 \ --namespace cert-manager \ --create-namespace \ --set crds.enabled=true \ --set global.leaderElection.namespace=cert-manager helm install alloydbomni-operator oci://gcr.io/alloydb-omni/alloydbomni-operator \ --version 1.9.0 \ --create-namespace \ --namespace alloydb-omni-system \ $(helm install --help | grep -q -- '--rollback-on-failure' && echo '--rollback-on-failure' || echo '--atomic') \ --timeout 5m"), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fefb76a8c90>)])]>

Step 2: Create your AlloyDB Omni database

Don’t forget to enable the googleMLExtension.

code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'kubectl create namespace ai-demo cat << \'EOF\' | kubectl apply -f - apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: db-pw-my-omni namespace: ai-demo type: Opaque data: my-omni: "VmVyeVN0cm9uZ1Bhc3N3b3Jk" # password "VeryStrongPassword" --- apiVersion: alloydbomni.dbadmin.goog/v1 kind: DBCluster metadata: name: my-omni namespace: ai-demo spec: databaseVersion: "18.4.0" primarySpec: adminUser: passwordRef: name: db-pw-my-omni features: googleMLExtension: enabled: true resources: cpu: 2 memory: 4Gi disks: - name: DataDisk size: 20Gi storageClass: standard dbLoadBalancerOptions: annotations: networking.gke.io/load-balancer-type: "internal" allowExternalIncomingTraffic: true EOF'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fefb76aa250>)])]>

Step 3: Deploy your AI model

We will use Ollama to help us deploy our model.

In this example we deploy Gemma 4 from Google DeepMind. Or, you can modify this command to deploy Qwen3.8 – just change a few lines as noted in the comments.

code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'cat << \'EOF\' | kubectl apply -f - apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: ollama namespace: ai-demo spec: replicas: 1 selector: matchLabels: app: ollama template: metadata: labels: app: ollama spec: containers: - name: ollama image: ollama/ollama:latest ports: - containerPort: 11434 env: - name: OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE value: "-1" # keep the model in RAM - name: OLLAMA_LOAD_TIMEOUT value: "20m" resources: requests: cpu: "4" memory: "16Gi" # for Qwen 3.8: 24Gi volumeMounts: - name: models mountPath: /root/.ollama lifecycle: postStart: exec: command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "(sleep 5 && ollama pull gemma4:12b) >/dev/null 2>&1 &"] # For Qwen 3.8, comment out the line above and use this one: # command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "(sleep 5 && ollama pull qwen3.8) >/dev/null 2>&1 &"] volumes: - name: models ephemeral: volumeClaimTemplate: spec: accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"] resources: requests: storage: 30Gi --- apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: name: ollama-service namespace: ai-demo spec: type: ClusterIP ports: - port: 11434 targetPort: 11434 selector: app: ollama EOF'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fefb76a9550>)])]>

Step 4: Register the model with AlloyDB Omni

Connect to your database.

code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'kubectl exec -it -n ai-demo $(kubectl get pod -n ai-demo -l alloydbomni.internal.dbadmin.goog/task-type=database -o jsonpath=\'{.items[0].metadata.name}\') -c database -- env PGPASSWORD="VeryStrongPassword" psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fefb76a9ed0>)])]>

Note: If you receive a connection error, you might need to wait a moment for your database to provision.

Now you should be connected to your AlloyDB Omni database with the psql client. Next, run the following SQL script to register your local model.

code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS google_ml_integration; ALTER SYSTEM SET google_ml_integration.request_timeout_in_seconds = 600; SELECT pg_reload_conf(); CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION google_ml.ollama_llm_input_transform( model_id character varying, prompt text, generation_config json, system_instructions json ) RETURNS json AS $$ SELECT json_build_object( 'model', CASE model_id WHEN 'gemma4_llm' THEN 'gemma4:12b' WHEN 'qwen3_8_llm' THEN 'qwen3.8' END, 'messages', json_build_array( json_build_object('role', 'system', 'content', COALESCE(system_instructions->'systemInstruction'->'parts'->0->>'text', 'You are a helpful assistant.')), json_build_object('role', 'user', 'content', prompt) ) ); $$ LANGUAGE sql; CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION google_ml.ollama_llm_output_transform( model_id character varying, response json ) RETURNS text AS $$ SELECT trim(regexp_replace( response->'choices'->0->'message'->>'content', '<think>.*?</think>', '', 's')); $$ LANGUAGE sql; CALL google_ml.create_model( model_id => 'gemma4_llm', -- and/or 'qwen3_8_llm', model_request_url => 'http://ollama-service.ai-demo.svc.cluster.local:11434/v1/chat/completions', model_provider => 'custom', model_type => 'llm', model_in_transform_fn => 'google_ml.ollama_llm_input_transform', model_out_transform_fn => 'google_ml.ollama_llm_output_transform' );"), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fefb76a8550>)])]>

Note: If you receive a Resource not found error, wait a moment for the model to load.

In addition to registering your model, the above script tells AlloyDB Omni how to interpret the model’s raw output. In this example chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning is part of the response inside <think></think> tags. We don’t want the CoT, so our output transform function removes it.

Step 5: Try it out!

You can use functions like ai.generate built-in to AlloyDB Omni to connect to your local model – without ever leaving the SQL client!

code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', "CREATE TABLE customer_feedback ( id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, customer_name TEXT, comment TEXT ); INSERT INTO customer_feedback (customer_name, comment) VALUES ('Alice', 'I was charged twice on my credit card! Please refund $49 immediately or I will cancel.'), ('Bob', 'Great product, but can you please add dark mode support?'); SELECT customer_name, ai.generate('Summarize in 1 short sentence: ' || comment, model_id => 'gemma4_llm' /* or 'qwen3_8_llm' */) AS summary FROM customer_feedback;"), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fefb76aaa90>)])]>

Make it your own

Try out all the AI features that AlloyDB Omni has to offer! AlloyDB Omni supports fast vector search, built-in AI functions, and more. Give them a try and build something great.

items.title: claude-code v2.1.329
items.summary:
What's changed

  • Added a trust dialog warning that says where a folder's hooks are declared
  • Added a warning in the conversation, in Claude Desktop and other non-interactive hosts, when hooks in managed settings fail to load
  • Added this session's scheduled tasks, /loop wakeups, the goal and this conversation's forks to /tasks; x stops one after asking
  • Added a "Server message" row to a server's page in /mcp that shows the JSON-RPC error message of a remote HTTP MCP server that refuses the connection
  • Added a "Marketplace auto-update" row to /status that names managed marketplaces that get no automatic updates, and why
  • Added support for turning on Code Mode while OpenTelemetry events and metrics are enabled; each tool call the code makes sends its events; tracing still keeps it off
  • Fixed ~/.claude.json sometimes being reset to defaults when a network stall or file lock made it unreadable and cleared during a save
  • Fixed repeated sign-outs on macOS when Claude Code could read the Keychain but not save to it. That session now stops at expiry and says why, and other sessions stay signed in
  • Fixed /terminal-setup corrupting VS Code settings or keybindings files around block comments, and reporting success while losing the Shift+Enter binding where keybindings.json has an unclosed string
  • Fixed files accepted through the IDE diff being saved without their last newline, and losing their byte order mark (BOM) when an edit was accepted by saving the diff in VS Code
  • Fixed picking a cloud session in /teleport replacing your open conversation: the pick now starts a new session, as /clear does, and /resume brings the old one back
  • Fixed /usage-credits asking Pro and Max users to log in again after opening the browser, and the link disappearing after 8 seconds if the browser doesn't open and a task stops for usage credits
  • Fixed /usage saying usage credits are off when they had run out or reached the monthly limit, and /model not telling Pro and Max users when that limit blocks a model that runs on usage credits
  • Fixed the spend limit menu showing your spend as your monthly limit and wrapping its rows under the pointer in narrow windows
  • Fixed a status line script that prints without end freezing the prompt and using gigabytes of memory
  • Fixed an empty, frozen screen after approving managed settings while the --resume picker, the trust dialog or another set-up screen was waiting
  • Fixed choosing Default in /model replacing your saved model with your organization's default when the Default row already showed your saved model
  • Fixed an MCP server being signed in again after you cleared its authentication while a token refresh was running
  • Fixed background MCP tasks that stalled after a slow reconnect: Claude Code now reconnects most HTTP MCP servers by itself when one is left on an older protocol version
  • Fixed PDFs, images and .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files that MCP servers or websites send as application/octet-stream being saved as .bin, which kept Claude from reading the PDFs and images
  • Fixed /code-review <pr number> sometimes reviewing the checked-out branch instead of the pull request without saying so: it now reads the pull request with gh pr diff, or says when it can't
  • Fixed /code-review stopping at a permission prompt, on most models, to look for a ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md that doesn't exist
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed --push-outcome-on-release sometimes deleting a session's branch on the git host
  • Fixed Code Mode hiding a script's finished edits and the stopped command after Esc, and losing them on exit
  • Fixed a runaway loop in Code Mode filling the machine's memory; it is now stopped at a limit
  • Fixed a background agent running on when it was stopped while it was being resumed
  • Fixed background shell commands using memory for the earlier conversation until they exit
  • Fixed Remote Control using memory for the earlier conversation after a compaction or /clear in sessions run by Claude Desktop, IDEs or the SDK
  • Fixed Stop not ending a request in Claude Desktop sessions on Bedrock while it waits on a hung AWS credential_process or sign-in call
  • Fixed Claude sometimes failing to send you a file on its first try on Opus 4.8 and Opus 5
  • Fixed Claude not being told that a connected MCP server's tools could not be loaded, and taking it for a server with no tools, in sessions with tool search
  • Fixed claude mcp login and /mcp saying a service doesn't accept sign-ins from Claude Code when the service's client registration had been retired (HTTP 410 Gone)
  • Fixed another case of claude.ai-synced plugin hooks failing with "Plugin directory does not exist" while a session was still running on macOS
  • Fixed auto mode asking for manual approval to rm a symlink that points outside the working directory or at itself
  • Fixed /sandbox on Linux listing allowUnixSockets entries as allowed: they don't open those sockets there, and /sandbox now says so
  • Fixed pressing Esc twice to clear a mistyped code ending the sign-in in /install-github-app
  • Remote Control: Fixed sessions going back to their first effort level after a restart while the app still showed the level you picked (not yet for sessions that start in Ultracode)
  • Fixed a removed plugin's MCP server staying connected in headless sessions after reload_plugins or when the account's plugin list drops it
  • Fixed the Claude Docs connector's tools going missing when a plugin or MCP server at the same address failed to connect, and its error wrongly suggesting /login
  • Fixed a new skills, commands or agents folder being missed when --add-dir names the working directory or Claude Code starts in the home folder
  • Fixed sessions started from a pre-warmed process ignoring the autoCompactWindow setting in the project's .claude/settings.json
  • Fixed CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE staying in effect in a running session after it is removed from settings.json
  • Fixed the Agent tool's effort parameter being ignored for named teammates in agent teams
  • Fixed /auto-mode-setup ignoring recent auto mode denials when it scans a project for rules to suggest; it may now offer allow rules from them, and you review each before it's saved
  • Fixed a false "Couldn't save this change" warning after adding a permission rule or directory in a subfolder or worktree whose own .claude/settings.local.json is unreadable or malformed
  • Fixed cloud sessions telling Claude to run a network proxy check after a failed request, which auto mode then blocked
  • Fixed headless rewind and fork going ahead while a message sent right after a model change still waited on it
  • Fixed Claude not being told when a background task was stopped while a cloud session was restarting
  • Fixed /team-onboarding reporting a guide as shared on Team and Enterprise plans when the server refused the upload
  • Fixed panels and questions being cut off at the prompt in fullscreen, /help, history search and the background tasks list losing rows or titles in short windows, and tables wrapping in dialogs
  • Fixed resumed sessions showing "Rejected" or "Declined" for edits, questions and plans that were cut off when the session ended
  • Fixed /passes showing the wrong number of passes after a server error, and offering usage credits for sharing when no guest passes are left
  • Fixed claude --help output being cut short when piped to another program
  • Fixed /terminal-setup turning on "Use Option as Meta key" in Terminal.app on macOS 27, and tips there suggesting Option+Enter instead of Shift+Enter
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed setup failing on Git LFS repositories cloned through Anthropic-managed git; sessions now start on pointer files, and git lfs pull fetches the content
  • Fixed sessions on self-hosted environments not starting from a git remote with an SSH host alias, GitHub SSH certificates or a GHE.com SSH user; an unresolved alias's error gives two git commands
  • Fixed remote MCP servers in self-hosted runner sessions staying without tools, or (over https) disconnected, after a timeout or network error
  • Fixed self-hosted runner sessions being shown as having stopped responding while Claude Code was still starting
  • Fixed Code Mode keeping in memory every large text file that code read, and memory growing each time a background subagent was woken
  • Fixed Code Mode stopping a script at its ten-minute limit while an MCP form, an MCP link prompt or a prompt that always asks was waiting for an answer
  • Fixed Code Mode scripts receiving a "moved to the background" message as data from most MCP calls over two minutes: the script now waits up to ten minutes, then gets an error
  • Fixed mods that list only some tools silently turning Code Mode off; such a mod no longer keeps it off, so use managed settings for that
  • Fixed Code Mode ignoring an MCP tool's request to end the turn when the tool was called from a script that Claude waits for
  • Fixed a Code Mode script's let x; keeping the value that an earlier script gave x
  • Fixed a Code Mode script's call with no argument failing with a missing-parameter error on tools that need none
  • Fixed Code Mode scripts losing access to tools through tools in sessions with more than 4,096 tools
  • Fixed the /code-review findings card often showing "high" for a review that ran at medium, on most models
  • Fixed key hints in permission prompts, questions, /model and /rewind ignoring keybindings.json
  • Fixed auto-scroll, the PR status badge, the auto-compact warning and the ultracode tag not following the /config switches that control them in a running session
  • Fixed a custom cancel key not working in /add-dir, /tui feedback and the save-workflow form
  • Fixed arrow keys in the save-workflow form moving the selection in the workflow view behind it
  • Fixed /config saying nothing, or "dismissed", after changing many settings
  • Fixed Read and @-mentions showing one line too many for files that end in a newline
  • Fixed /status not naming the model that opusplan and haiku use in plan mode
  • Fixed claude doctor advising a Keychain unlock inside a macOS sandbox, where unlocking can't help
  • Fixed the "Jump to bottom" pill staying hidden after copying text and scrolling away, the row under it going blank when its label changed, and quick PageUp presses scrolling too far in fullscreen
  • Fixed a screen update sometimes being skipped when memory is low
  • Fixed long code blocks losing a blank line and repeating another in scrollback
  • Fixed prompt suggestions sometimes showing placeholder text such as _(no suggestion)_
  • Fixed the line about earlier messages on resume blaming a damaged file when the file was intact
  • Fixed characters disappearing from the prompt when its text held a color code that sets several styles and a keyword or command was highlighted
  • Fixed /rename and UserPromptSubmit hook titles in claude remote-control sessions not showing on claude.ai and mobile
  • Fixed the Remote Control diff listing a file twice when the branch renamed it and it was then edited
  • Improved the automatic clean-up of old sessions on computers with managed settings
  • Improved /tui and other in-place restarts to wait briefly for a login refresh, so they are less likely to sign you out
  • Improved memory use in long sessions that edit many files, and in long Claude Desktop sessions on macOS and Linux with many large MCP tool results
  • Windows: Improved start-up and the first search on PCs where Claude Code's search program starts slowly
  • Improved auto mode's handling of a short reply such as "yes" to Claude's question when telemetry is off, behind a gateway to the Anthropic API, or on Microsoft Foundry
  • Improved memory use of idle Claude Desktop and SDK sessions after a long turn, and after --resume or --continue of a session that holds screenshots or large tool results
  • Improved how fast a Claude Desktop Code session with Remote Control on is ready for the next message after an answer
  • Improved cloud sessions to retry plugins that failed to download at startup
  • Improved Code Mode: the terminal freezes for far less time after a script makes thousands of tool calls
  • Improved Code Mode: after starting a subagent, Claude now gets the same guidance on waiting as outside Code Mode
  • Updated computer use on macOS to newer safety rules, so some actions are refused and some apps have less access
  • Changed saved scheduled tasks: in new signed-in sessions, most saved by earlier versions need scheduling again, though --resume of their own session still runs them
  • Changed /code-review with no target on most models to review the whole branch against the default branch, and fixed it losing the diff on multi-commit branches
  • Changed auto mode to run git status less often so most requests wait less in large repositories; a git command that discards changes may be blocked until the working tree is checked
  • Changed /code-review <pr number> --fix, and /code-review given a pull request URL, to stop without reviewing when gh pr diff is refused or fails
  • Changed 'Exit and stop tasks' to end this session's scheduled tasks so they don't run again on resume, unless you exit while Claude is responding
  • Changed some teammate panes to start through /bin/sh, so they may not read shell start-up files
  • Changed computer use on macOS to give up on an app launch that has not finished after 30 seconds
  • Gateway: Changed the start-up warning shown while access_control.allow_cidrs is empty to a notice at every start, boxed in text logs: never expose the gateway to the public internet
  • Self-hosted runner: Changed a second host name's clone of the same owner/name to go under _repos/clones/<host>/ in the base folder; no clone moves
  • Self-hosted runner: Changed repositories with unusual characters in their address path to clone anew in a new folder; rules and volumes naming the old one stop applying, and the old clone stays put
  • Self-hosted runner: Changed --repository-folder to take most folders in the base folder at --capacity 1 (above 1, one there stops start-up); another repository's session overlapping one is refused
  • Changed Code Mode so a PreToolUse hook that errors no longer refuses a script's tool call, as outside Code Mode; set "onFailure": "block" on a command, HTTP or MCP tool hook that must refuse
  • Changed Code Mode to refuse a script's read of a line range over 256 MiB, which could use gigabytes of memory, and fixed reads of very long lines timing out
  • Changed Code Mode to also start when telemetry, nonessential traffic or feature flags are turned off; an administrator can keep it off in managed settings
  • Changed Code Mode to run a script that declares its own log, preview or sleep, which it used to refuse
  • Changed macOS login renewal to test the Keychain with a Claude Code-write-check item
  • Changed the /tasks header and the footer's background count to one number covering shells, monitors, MCP calls, agents, workflows and scheduled tasks
  • Changed Stop and SubagentStop hooks to list a Monitor's script as monitor, not shell, in background_tasks
  • Removed 2.1.326's automatic retry at the limit named in a max_tokens error; behind a gateway whose model takes fewer output tokens, set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS to that limit
  • [VSCode] Added a line above the message box after you decline the trust prompt, with Review trust to bring the prompt back without reloading the window
  • [VSCode] Fixed being signed out of Claude Code in every window and terminal when the sign-in server took 10 to 30 seconds to answer the extension's token refresh
  • [VSCode] Fixed keys pressed while an input method (IME) is composing moving focus on or declining a permission prompt, running menu rows and closing dialogs (#106358)
  • [VSCode] Fixed the permission prompt for Bash, Edit, Write and other built-in tools not showing why a safety check asks
  • [VSCode] Fixed a half-written plan comment being lost or moved to another passage, and an input method's Enter sending the comment, ending a session rename or picking an @-mentioned file
  • [VSCode] Fixed the limit banner not saying when usage credits are in use, and the session survey covering that banner and the usage credits card
  • [VSCode] Fixed screen readers not announcing a permission request that arrived while the Account & Usage dialog was open until that dialog was closed
  • [VSCode] Fixed a proposed-edit diff tab staying open, with an Accept button that did nothing, after its terminal Claude Code session disconnected
  • [VSCode] Fixed short tool inputs and outputs cut off at the panel's edge with no way to read the rest (they now open in an editor tab), and dragging to select text also opening one
  • [VSCode] Fixed the Up key putting an earlier message over text that an input method (IME) is composing in the message box (#101294)
  • [VSCode] Fixed dropping an Explorer folder onto the chat inserting nothing on VS Code 1.103 to 1.139 or in a floating chat window, and the drop highlight vanishing with a false "Hold Shift" hint
  • [VSCode] Fixed a permission prompt moving keyboard focus away from the details you were scrolling as its buttons switched on
  • [VSCode] Fixed file links in a Claude tab opening in another editor group when claudeCode.lockEditorGroups is off (#108884)
  • [VSCode] Fixed ranges written with a single tilde (3~5 … 7~10) losing their tildes and showing struck-through text between them; only ~~text~~ is struck through now
  • [VSCode] Fixed dictation errors wrapping into a narrow column, the spinner turning while a question card waits, and a NUL symbol after each letter in the output of a failed UTF-16 command
  • [VSCode] Changed Down to stop at the last item of a permission prompt instead of wrapping to Yes
  • [VSCode] Changed command output to show hidden characters and control sequences other than plain colors as symbols, so Persian, Khmer, Lao, Sinhala and Malayalam text can look broken or out of order
